scope_summary: Primer application for interior trim (baseboard, door casing, window casing, other trim) in new construction. Covers substrate-specific primer selection: factory-primed trim (optional additional primer), bare MDF (solvent-based edge sealer + latex face primer), bare FJP (stain-blocking primer required), bare solid wood (standard primer-sealer), and glossy/oil-based existing substrates (bonding primer). Primer requirement is driven by substrate_condition dimension, NOT quality tier. Uses LF as primary UOM per PDCA standard (1 LF trim = 1 SF). This spec is PRIME ONLY - finish coats belong to SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT.
relevant_findings: Primer requirement is driven by substrate condition and system specification, NOT quality tier (Fine_Finish_Doctrine Section 2.1 - mandatory doctrine)

MDF edges MUST receive solvent-based sealer (shellac or oil-based) before ANY latex products. Water-based primers cause irreversible fiber raise on MDF edges. This creates a two-step process for bare MDF.
FJP (Finger-Joint Pine) REQUIRES stain-blocking primer. Without stain-blocking, resin bleed-through will appear as amber/yellow discoloration within weeks/months. This is non-negotiable for bare FJP.
Factory primer on pre-primed trim is transit protection, not finish-ready prep. Per Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine Section 2.3: factory primer is often thin and may have handling damage.
Per PDCA standard, each LF of trim is counted as 1 SF regardless of actual width (Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine Section 1.3)
Brush is the NC production standard for trim priming. Spray requires wall protection but is faster for large scope (Fine_Finish_Doctrine Section 15.1.1).
Profile complexity modifiers per Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine Section 7.2: Simple=0.85x, Standard=1.0x, Complex=1.25x, Ornate=1.40x
In NC sequence, trim is typically installed AFTER walls are primed but BEFORE walls are finish painted
Quality tier controls inspection/repair scrutiny, NOT primer selection or application quality
Trim joints (miters, copes, scarf joints) require caulking - approximately 1 joint per 8-12 LF of trim
Casing end grain exposures require grain fill - typically 2 per door opening, 4 per window opening
Floor protection is conditional on floor_type site condition - subfloor may require no protection
Glossy/oil-based existing substrates require adhesion testing and bonding primer

condition_drivers.impact: Primary driver for primer system selection. Each substrate type requires different primer chemistry and may require multiple steps (e.g., MDF edge seal + face prime).
User configuration whether to apply additional primer coat on factory-primed trim. Factory primer is transit protection, often thin.
Drives inspection/repair intensity and scrutiny level. Does NOT affect primer selection. QT3=quick glance at 6ft, QT4=systematic scan at 3ft, QT5=lighted critical at arm's length.
Brush is NC production standard. Spray requires wall protection but faster for large volume. Both must achieve QT standards.
Affects production rates. More complex profiles require more time per LF.
Affects production via height modifiers. Standard (7-8ft) = H1, Tall (9-12ft) = H2, High (13ft+) = H3.

failure_modes.cause: Applying water-based primer to raw MDF edges before solvent-based sealer
failure_modes.prevention: ALWAYS seal MDF edges with shellac-based or oil-based sealer FIRST, then apply latex primer to faces
failure_modes.reversibility: Difficult - requires sanding back to substrate

failure_modes.prevention: ALWAYS use stain-blocking primer on bare FJP (shellac-based like BIN, or high-quality acrylic stain-blocking like KILZ 3)
failure_modes.reversibility: Difficult - bleed may re-emerge through multiple finish coats

failure_modes.cause: Painting over glossy or oil-based existing finish without proper prep and bonding primer
failure_modes.prevention: Adhesion test, thorough degloss/sand, and bonding primer (STIX, BIN, or equivalent)

failure_modes.cause: Factory primer contaminated with oils, wax, or silicone from handling/shipping
failure_modes.prevention: Scuff sand factory-primed surfaces and clean with tack cloth before additional primer or finish
failure_modes.reversibility: Spot scrape and reprime affected areas

failure_modes.cause: FJP finger joints moving and showing through finish over time
failure_modes.prevention: High-build primer, multiple coats, proper joint sealing

failure_modes.cause: Water-based primer raising wood grain on bare softwood
failure_modes.prevention: Accept first coat grain raise, sand smooth before additional coats. Expected behavior.

failure_modes.cause: Water-based primer over bare nail heads causing rust spots
failure_modes.prevention: Spot-prime fastener heads with shellac or oil-based primer before full coat (mostly repaint concern)

substrate_specific_requirements.notes: Factory primer is transit protection. Additional primer recommended for quality work but user-configurable.

substrate_specific_requirements.primer_type: Two-step: (1) Solvent-based sealer on EDGES ONLY, (2) High-build latex on FACES
substrate_specific_requirements.notes: MDF edge sealing is MANDATORY. Water-based primers cause irreversible fiber raise on MDF edges. Edges require solvent-based sealer (shellac or oil-based) BEFORE any latex. Faces can receive latex primer after edge seal.
FJP stain-blocking is MANDATORY. Without stain-blocking, resin bleed will occur. Shellac-based (BIN) or high-quality acrylic stain-blocking (KILZ 3) required. Standard primers will NOT block resin.

prep_required: Spot prime knots with shellac if present
substrate_specific_requirements.notes: Standard softwood (pine, poplar) requires basic primer-sealer. Knots may require shellac spot prime for stain blocking.
Glossy surfaces have low porosity - degloss and bonding primer required for adhesion.
Oil-based/alkyd finishes require adhesion testing and bonding primer. Latex over oil can fail without proper bonding primer.

valid_input_states.rationale: NC trim arrives as factory-primed (most common) or bare. Remodel/addition scenarios may encounter existing painted trim. Each input state drives primer selection.

output_state.rationale: All substrate scenarios output field-primed state, ready for finish coats. This is the target state for SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT input.

adjacent_state_protection_analysis.rationale: In typical NC sequence, walls are primed but not finish painted during trim prime. No wall protection needed for brush. Spray requires light_mask at wall-trim edge. If walls are already finish painted (atypical), full protection required.
Floor protection via perimeter drops when finished floors present. No protection needed on subfloor.

notes_for_materials_manager: Material selection is SUBSTRATE-DRIVEN per Fine_Finish_Doctrine Section 2.1 - this is mandatory doctrine
MDF edges: Solvent-based sealer ONLY (shellac-based like Zinsser BIN, or oil-based like KILZ Original). Water-based causes fiber raise.
MDF faces: High-build latex primer (ProClassic Undercoater, Fresh Start 046)
FJP: Stain-blocking primer MANDATORY (Zinsser BIN Shellac, KILZ 3, Cover Stain). Non-stain-blocking primers WILL fail on FJP.
Bare solid wood: Standard acrylic primer-sealer (Zinsser Bulls Eye 1-2-3, KILZ 2). Spot prime knots with shellac if present.
Glossy/oil existing: Bonding primer (Zinsser STIX, BIN, XIM UMA)
Factory primed (if adding primer): High-build latex undercoater
Coverage rates per Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine: ~400-500 LF/gal for standard primer
Caulk: Paintable acrylic latex caulk for all trim joints
Filler: Lightweight spackling for fastener holes, wood filler for grain fill on end grain
notes_for_sop_librarian: Module structure follows Fine Finish pattern: MOD_FF_SETUP, MOD_FF_INITIAL_PREP, MOD_FF_PRIME, MOD_FF_CLEANUP
NO interstage or finish modules in prime spec - those belong to SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT
Substrate condition dimension drives which primer tasks are included
MDF requires TWO prime tasks: TSK_TRIM_SEAL_MDF_EDGES (solvent-based) + TSK_TRIM_PRIME_MDF_FACES (latex)
FJP requires stain-blocking primer task - NOT optional, NOT configurable
Task IDs should use TSK_TRIM_PRIME_* prefix
Fill fastener holes task: TSK_TRIM_FILL_FASTENERS (use LF heuristic: 2 holes per 12-16 inches)
Caulk joints task: TSK_TRIM_CAULK_JOINTS (all miter/cope/scarf joints)
Grain fill task: TSK_TRIM_FILL_GRAIN (end grain on bare wood casings)
Inspection/repair intensity is QT-scaled but primer application is binary (same at all tiers)
Floor protection tasks conditional on floor_type site condition
Wall masking tasks conditional on application_method = spray
